task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of September 8, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about remote workers using the old Celandine schoolroom as shared workspace and the practical limits of selling a quiet place to work.

facts.text: An August 2026 room-use note records customer-service worker Tara Veyne moving from a shared desk into a reserved booth before starting a scheduled call.
Celandine Workroom occupies a former school classroom and provides 12 desks and four enclosed call booths.
A day pass costs $12; booth time must be reserved but carries no extra charge within the pass's stated daily allowance.
The operator also sells a monthly $80 pass permitting up to 12 visits, rather than unlimited attendance.
Forty-six people hold monthly passes, but the room cannot seat all of them at the same time.
In a supplied full working week, 210 desk-hours were booked out of 600 offered, an overall booking rate of 35%.
The weekly average masks busier Tuesday and Thursday periods and does not measure booth occupancy.
Veyne uses the workroom when building repairs make her home unsuitable for calls; her employer permits customer calls only from an enclosed booth in this shared setting.
No customer call content, account details or employer credentials are included in the reporting notes.
Veyne said, "I am not buying another office identity. I am buying a room where I can finish this day's work."
Operator Omi Lerren says booth demand can be high even when several desks are empty.
Lerren said, "A free chair does not solve a booking problem when everybody needs to talk at once."
The operator estimates that the backup unit can power the essential network equipment for about 45 minutes, not all desks and appliances.
A power backup does not guarantee that an external broadband-provider outage will be resolved.
The operator recorded three service interruptions in the first quarter but has not supplied a comparison proving better reliability than every user's home connection.
A town start-up grant pays part of the first year's rent and ends in December.
The operator has not published a complete break-even calculation or secured replacement grant funding.
Users include employees, freelancers and people completing administrative work for small businesses, not one uniform occupational group.
The former classroom's blackboard remains on one wall and is used for room notices rather than recording clients' work.
No plan has been approved to convert the entire former school into offices or add residential accommodation.

forbidden_additions: Unlimited monthly access, simultaneous space for all members or guaranteed connectivity
Private customer details, verified profitability or funded expansion of the whole school
